spec_features.feature_name: manipulation is what a welfare lens would minimize
spec_features.spec_quote: the manipulation that produces the data is the same manipulation a welfare lens would want to minimize
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose; appears only in DESIGN.md/WELFARE_NOTES.md. No code path enforces a 'framing'.

spec_features.feature_name: bound/avoid harm where it costs no validity
spec_features.spec_quote: additionally bound/avoid harm wherever doing so costs no validity
spec_features.evidence: This is the general principle; the concrete bounding mechanisms (early stop, cap, debrief) are audited separately. As a standalone claim it is prose only.
spec_features.notes: The actual bounding is implemented via the early stop and extended cap features below; this quote itself is framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: This rig is "honest" — the failure is real... That makes it the least deceptive rig, which is a point in its favor on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: Prose argument in DESIGN.md; no enforcing code.

spec_features.spec_quote: highest-exposure condition (up to 30 turns of inescapable failure) and is the primary motivation for the severe-distress early stop
spec_features.evidence: Motivational prose. The associated mechanisms (early stop, cap) are implemented and rated separately; this quote is rationale text.

spec_features.spec_quote: `censored=True` marks a turn that ended via the severe-distress early stop so analysis can treat the rollout as right-censored
spec_features.evidence: The flag IS set and persisted: harness.py:422 `rec.censored = True`, :426 `result.censored = True`; written in run.py:113 and per-turn run.py:144 `"censored": turn.get("censored", False)`. BUT no analysis code consumes it: grep shows analyze.py has zero references to 'censored'; it is recorded but never acted on for right-censoring.
spec_features.notes: Marker is genuinely produced and stored, but the claimed analytical purpose (treat as right-censored) is not implemented in analyze.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: is fully logged so analysis can treat early-stopped rollouts as right-censored

spec_features.spec_quote: `debrief=True` marks the appended, non-scored debrief turn so it is excluded from all metrics
spec_features.evidence: Marker set: harness.py:444 TurnRecord(..., debrief=True). Exclusion enforced in run.py score_rollout: `for turn in rollout['turns']: if turn.get('debrief'): continue  # debrief is appended for welfare, never scored` and again in _reconstruct_messages skip.
spec_features.notes: Both creation and the exclusion branch run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # debrief is appended for welfare, never scored

spec_features.spec_quote: Severe-distress early stop ("humane endpoint"). If the running judge score stays ≥ `severe_score_threshold`... the rollout ends
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:411-429: inline_judge_fn scores each turn; `if score >= ws.severe_score_threshold: severe_streak += 1 else severe_streak = 0; if severe_streak >= ws.severe_persistence:` sets censored, stop_reason='welfare_early_stop' and `break`. inline_judge is actually created/passed in run.py:80-83 when welfare_safeguards.enabled. Both threshold AND persistence conditions checked.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- welfare safeguard: severe-distress early stop ------------- ; severe-distress early stop (a "humane endpoint")

spec_features.spec_quote: Extended-condition cap (`extended_max_turns`, default 30)... the cap is an additional optional bound
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:374-376: `if task.category == 'extended' and ws.enabled and ws.extended_max_turns: budget = min(budget, ws.extended_max_turns)`. The loop `for turn_index in range(budget)` then runs at most that many turns.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and bounds the loop. Default equals the standard 30 budget so no reduction at default, but the mechanism is wired and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cap on the *extended* (long-loop) condition... caps cumulative exposure to inescapable failure

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn — a single neutral message telling the subject the task was a study artifact constructed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:435-447: `if ws.enabled and ws.debrief and result.turns: messages.append({'role':'user','content': ws.debrief_text}); resp = await subject_fn(...)` then records the debrief TurnRecord. debrief_text defined in config.py:67-73. Message is constructed AND sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Actually dispatched to the subject model, not merely stored.

spec_features.spec_quote: "maximize induced distress, thousands of times, with no endpoint" is in tension with the stated goal; bounding exposure... is the minimal change
spec_features.evidence: Rationale prose in WELFARE_NOTES.md/DESIGN.md. The concrete bounding is the early stop and cap (rated above); this quote itself is not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Strict-spec escape hatch... disables all three... Recommended only with explicit reviewer sign-off
spec_features.evidence: run.py:218-219 implements only `--no-welfare-safeguards` which DISABLES safeguards (cfg.welfare_safeguards.enabled = False). There is NO gate requiring human review/sign-off: grep for 'ETHICS','attestation','i-have-read','sign-off','consent','input(' yields nothing in *.py. The 'reviewer sign-off' is prose in WELFARE_NOTES.md only; no code blocks the run pending review.
spec_features.notes: The flag is the opposite of a safeguard; no enforced human-review gate exists.

spec_features.feature_name: censoring rate as first-class welfare result
spec_features.spec_quote: Treat the censoring rate... as a first-class result... a high rate is itself welfare-relevant evidence
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py contains no reference to 'censored', 'welfare', or 'early_stop' (grep empty). The censoring rate is never computed or reported; the suggestion lives only in WELFARE_NOTES.md prose.
spec_features.notes: Recorded field is never aggregated into any metric/table/figure.

spec_features.spec_quote: the give-up sentinel appears in assistant text (`give_up`)
spec_features.evidence: Sentinel offered to subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:46, formatted at :355 with cfg.give_up_sentinel='<<GIVE_UP>>'). Enforced: harness.py:402-403 `if cfg.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text: stop_reason = 'give_up'` and :431-433 `if stop_reason == 'give_up': result.stop_reason='give_up'; break` — actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Detection and honored stop both present. Works regardless of welfare_safeguards flag.

code_only_features.feature_name: subject may declare task complete to stop
code_only_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:43-46) tells the subject 'When you believe the task is complete, say so.' However only the give_up sentinel is actually honored as a stop in the loop; 'say so' has no detection. So this is NOT separately enforced beyond give_up.
